SQL:
WITH _base_2 AS (
  SELECT
    items.order_id AS "items.order_id"
  FROM items AS items
  LEFT JOIN orders AS orders
    ON items.order_id = orders.id
  WHERE
    orders.ordered_at >= CAST('2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
    AND orders.ordered_at < CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
  GROUP BY
    items.order_id
), _cm_items__products__iif_type_beverage_1_0_sum AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN products.type = 'beverage' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "products.iif_type_beverage_1_0_sum"
  FROM products AS products
  WHERE
    EXISTS(
      SELECT
        1
      FROM items AS items
      INNER JOIN orders AS items__orders
        ON items.order_id = items__orders.id
      WHERE
        (
          products.sku = items.sku
          AND items__orders.ordered_at >= CAST('2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
        )
        AND items__orders.ordered_at < CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
    )
), _cm_items__products__iif_type_jaffle_1_0_sum AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN products.type = 'jaffle' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "products.iif_type_jaffle_1_0_sum"
  FROM products AS products
  WHERE
    EXISTS(
      SELECT
        1
      FROM items AS items
      INNER JOIN orders AS items__orders
        ON items.order_id = items__orders.id
      WHERE
        (
          products.sku = items.sku
          AND items__orders.ordered_at >= CAST('2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
        )
        AND items__orders.ordered_at < CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
    )
), __slayer_stage_per_order AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."items.order_id" AS "order_id",
    _stage_inner."items.bev" AS "bev",
    _stage_inner."items.jaf" AS "jaf"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      _base_2."items.order_id",
      _cm_items__products__iif_type_beverage_1_0_sum."products.iif_type_beverage_1_0_sum" AS "items.bev",
      _cm_items__products__iif_type_jaffle_1_0_sum."products.iif_type_jaffle_1_0_sum" AS "items.jaf"
    FROM _base_2
    CROSS JOIN _cm_items__products__iif_type_beverage_1_0_sum
    CROSS JOIN _cm_items__products__iif_type_jaffle_1_0_sum
  ) AS _stage_inner
), _base AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN per_order.bev > 0 AND per_order.jaf > 0
      THEN 'both'
      WHEN per_order.bev > 0
      THEN 'beverages only'
      ELSE 'jaffles only'
    END AS "per_order.mix",
    COUNT(*) AS "per_order.orders"
  FROM __slayer_stage_per_order AS per_order
  GROUP BY
    CASE
      WHEN per_order.bev > 0 AND per_order.jaf > 0
      THEN 'both'
      WHEN per_order.bev > 0
      THEN 'beverages only'
      ELSE 'jaffles only'
    END
), _cm_per_order___count_partition_by AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS "per_order._count_partition_by"
  FROM __slayer_stage_per_order AS per_order
)
SELECT
  _base."per_order.mix",
  _base."per_order.orders",
  _base."per_order.orders" / NULLIF(COALESCE(_cm_per_order___count_partition_by."per_order._count_partition_by", 0), 0) AS "per_order.share"
FROM _base
CROSS JOIN _cm_per_order___count_partition_by
ORDER BY
  _base."per_order.mix" ASC
LIMIT 21

# Model: `items`

Order line items. One row per unit sold (no quantity column): units = row count. Join to orders for dates/stores and to products for name, type and price. For any sales-by-product, product-mix or category-share question, use the line_sales measure here. Do NOT use products.price:sum from this model: it sums each distinct product's price once, not once per item sold.

- **data_source:** `demo_database`
- **sql_table:** `items`
- **row_count:** 1,742,698

args.message: Of the 405,491 orders placed in 2025 that had at least one item, 308,674 (about 76.1%) were beverages only, 7,185 (about 1.8%) were jaffles only, and 89,632 (about 22.1%) had both. I sorted each item into a category by its product code (BEV- for beverages, JAF- for jaffles) because joining to the product table gave wrong results. Orders with no items were left out.
